content.text: I have enough to conclude. No restriction on IBM's business, purchasing, or development activities exists anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: If MSL suffers a substantially adverse change in its business, related to a reduction in IBM's Products requirements, including reductions of Products requirements due to migration to a competitive supplier, for the [*] from the Effective Date of this Agreement, MSL may terminate such number of Transferred Employees as it deems necessary.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding IBM, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). I checked the sections most likely to carry such a covenant: § 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720) creates only a purchase obligation for ordered Products with no requirements/exclusivity commitment; § 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995) and § 16.15 "Prohibited Suppliers" (p0319) restrict MSL, not IBM; and searches for "compete/competing/competitive", "exclusive", "sole/second source" and "IBM shall not" returned no restrictive covenant against us. The tangential hits are neutral or favourable to IBM: § 9.0(e) (p0186) expressly contemplates IBM reducing its Product requirements by migrating to a competitive supplier — confirming our freedom to dual-source; § 5.1(v) (p0116) is a mutual termination right on a change of control by a direct competitor; and the confidentiality agreement (p1491) preserves each party's freedom to provide competitive products and to supply the other's competitors. No redline is required.
